org.portico.bindings

Interface IConnection

  • All Known Implementing Classes:
    JGroupsConnection, JVMConnection

    public interface IConnection
    The Portico communications infrastructure is abstracted from the rest of the framework so that it can be swapped out/replaced with differing implementations without the core of Portico having to know anything about it. The IConnection interface defines the contract between connection implementations and the rest of the Portico framework. Messages are passed to and from the connection, how they are sent across a network is a matter entirely for the consideration of a given implementation.

    Remote Messages Received by the Connection

    When a connection receives an incoming message it should place it in the message queue of the LRC it is associated with (something like lrc.getState().getQueue().offer(msg)).

    No Argument Constructors

    Instances of the concrete class that conforms to IConnection are created dynamically from the class name using reflection. Each implementation MUST provide a public, no-arg constructor that will be used to create new instances of it during startup.

    Connection Lifecycle

    Following instantiation, the infrastructure will put the connection through the following lifecycle:

    1. configure(LRC,Map): Once an instance of a conforming implementation has been created, it will be asked to configure itself. Inside the provided Map will be a number of items the connection can use to achieve this task.
    2. connect(): This is the signal to the connection that it is time to start doing its work. At this point, the connection should connect to the RTI/federation through whatever protocol-specific means is necessary (this includes RTI discovery if required).
    3. disconnect(): When the kernel is shutting down, it will notify the connection that it is time to finish up through this method. At this point, the connection should disconnect and perform any cleanup that is necessary.

    HLA Bootstrapping Methods

    Each connection also must implement a number of basic HLA bootstrapping methods. These 4 calls (create federation, destroy federation, join federation, resign federation) are ones that generally require some sort of speical handling on the part of the connection. For example, when joining a federation the connection might need to attempt to establish a particular connection to some service on behalf of the federate. It might also need to tear this down on resign. As such, these requests are treated specially and separate methods are provided for them. If no special processing is required by a particular connection, it can just treat these particular calls the same.

    For more information on the communications architecture, see the documentation on the Portico wiki.

    • Method Detail

      • configure

        void configure(LRC lrc,
               Map<String,Object> properties)
        throws JConfigurationException
        This method is called by the Portico infrastructure during setup.

        Called right after the connection implementation has been instantiated. This gives the connection an opportunity to perform any setup it requires. If there is a problem (either with any configuration data it has located through the properties map or some other mechanism) then it should throw a JConfigurationException. The LRC into which the connection is being deployed can be obtained via this method.

        Throws:
        JConfigurationException

      • connect

        void connect()
      throws JRTIinternalError
        This method is called by the Portico infrastructure during setup.

        When it is time for the kernel to connect to the RTI/federate/etc... and to start accepting incoming messages, while being ready to send outgoing messages, this method is called. The connection implementations should use it to connect to network (or whatever communications mechanism is being used). This should include any discovery of remote components (such as the discovery of an RTI by federates).

        Throws:
        JRTIinternalError

      • disconnect

        void disconnect()
         throws JRTIinternalError
        This method is called by the Portico infrastructure during shutdown.

        When the kernel is ready to shutdown, it will call this method, signalling to the connection that it should disconnect and do any shutdown and cleanup necessary.

        Throws:
        JRTIinternalError

      • broadcast

        void broadcast(PorticoMessage message)
        throws Exception
        Broadcast the given message out to all participants in a federation asynchronously. As soon as the message has been received for processing or sent, this method is free to return. No response will be waited for.
        Parameters:
        message - The message to broadcast
        Throws:
        Exception - If there was an error when sending the message

      • broadcastAndSleep

        void broadcastAndSleep(PorticoMessage message)
                throws Exception
        This method should be used when a message has to be sent and then time for responses to be broadcast back is needed before moving on. In this case, the connection will broadcast the message and then sleep for an amount of time appropriate based on the underlying comms protocol in use. For example, the JVM connection won't sleep for long, but a connection sending information over a network should wait longer.
        Parameters:
        message - The message to broadcast
        Throws:
        Exception - If there was an error when sending the message

      • createFederation

        void createFederation(CreateFederation createMessage)
               throws Exception
        Do any special processing required to create a federation and process the request. If there is any kind of connection specific problem (or a problem creating the federation in the first place), throw an exception idicating so.
        Throws:
        Exception

      • destroyFederation

        void destroyFederation(DestroyFederation destoryMessage)
                throws Exception
        Do any special processing required to destroy a federation and process the request. If there is any kind of connection specific problem (or a problem destroying the federation in the first place), throw an exception idicating so.
        Throws:
        Exception

      • joinFederation

        ConnectedRoster joinFederation(JoinFederation joinMessage)
                        throws Exception
        Do any special processing required to join a federation and process the request. If there is any kind of connection specific problem (or a problem joining the federation in the first place), throw an exception idicating so. The return should be an instance of ConnectedRoster containing all the necessary information about the federation (local handle, remote federate handles, fom, etc...)
        Throws:
        Exception

      • resignFederation

        void resignFederation(ResignFederation resignMessage)
               throws Exception
        Do any special processing required to resign from a federation and process the request. If there is any kind of connection specific problem (or a problem resigning from the federation in the first place), throw an exception idicating so.
        Throws:
        Exception

      • listActiveFederations

        String[] listActiveFederations()
                        throws Exception
        Returns a list of all the federations currently active. The manner for fetching this will be binding-specific. If there is a problem locating this information, throw an exception.
        Throws:
        Exception
